report: 44-year-old female: Findings: Supratentorial and infratentorial parenchymal structures show normal signal intensity. No diffusion restriction suggesting acute infarction. Ventricular system and cortical sulci are within normal limits for age. No extra-axial collection. Impression: Normal brain MRI.

67-year-old male: Findings: Multiple T2 and FLAIR hyperintense foci are seen in the bilateral periventricular and deep white matter, consistent with chronic ischemic gliotic changes. Mild cortical atrophy with widening of the cortical sulci. No acute diffusion restriction. Impression: Chronic ischemic white matter disease. Age-related cortical atrophy.

31-year-old female: Clinical information: Headache. Findings: A 12 mm extra-axial lesion with broad dural attachment is seen along the left frontal convexity, showing homogeneous contrast enhancement. Mild mass effect on the adjacent gyrus without midline shift. Remaining parenchyma is unremarkable. Impression: Findings consistent with a small left frontal convexity meningioma.

58-year-old male: Findings: An area of diffusion restriction with corresponding low ADC values is present in the right middle cerebral artery territory involving the insular cortex. Loss of grey-white differentiation in the same region. No haemorrhagic transformation on susceptibility-weighted sequences. Impression: Acute right MCA territory infarction.

9-year-old female: Findings: Posterior fossa structures are normal. No hydrocephalus. Pituitary gland and sella are normal. Paranasal sinuses show mild mucosal thickening in the maxillary sinuses. Impression: No intracranial pathology. Mild maxillary sinusitis.
